extracted.intended_audience: media who regularly cover the NBA, team communications staff, and others seeking official information about NBA officiating
extracted.subtask_description: Official NBA media guide content describing officiating staff, resources for media, and procedural rules (notably the Coach's Challenge) for use by reporters, broadcasters, and team communications personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBA Official site resources
rubrics_metrics.description: NBA Official (http://nba.com/official) is your source for the latest news and information about the NBA officiating program. The site features the NBA Rulebook, NBA Video Rulebook and NBA Replay Archive. Last Two Minute Reports, referee game assignments and pool reporter transcripts are also available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site is presented as the authoritative resource for rules, replay archives and official reports; it is a primary source for media and teams seeking officiating information. For real-time rules clarifications, follow NBA Official on Twitter @NBAOfficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Rulebook microsite purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBA has relaunched its Video Rulebook microsite to serve as a resource to teams, media and fans with an explanation of the rules of the game through videos selected from NBA games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended audiences are teams, media and fans; the Video Rulebook provides visual explanations of rules via selected game clips. URL provided: https://videorulebook.nba.com/.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBA Media Central membership & access
rubrics_metrics.description: NBA Media Central (https://mediacentral.nba.com) is a password-protected website designed for media who regularly cover the NBA. Membership to the site includes easy access to box scores and statistics; team game notes; press releases; credential timelines; team logos; head shots of players, coaches, referees and league executives; original content; and information about the WNBA, NBA G League and NBA 2K League.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site is for credentialed/regular media; registration URL provided (https://mediacentral.nba.com/register/). Access is controlled (password-protected) and membership implies access to an array of media assets and official documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coach's Challenge — one challenge per team
rubrics_metrics.description: Each team is entitled to one challenge in the game (regardless of whether the challenge is successful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a per-game allotment; successful or unsuccessful outcome does not affect allotment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coach's Challenge — challengeable event types
rubrics_metrics.description: A team can use its challenge in the following instances: 1.) a called personal foul charged to its own team; 2.) a called out-of-bounds violation; or 3.) a called goaltending or basket interference violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only these categories of called events are eligible for challenge under the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coach's Challenge — timing for personal fouls
rubrics_metrics.description: A team can use its challenge on a called personal foul at any point in the game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal-foul challenges are not limited by game clock except as otherwise specified for other event types in late-game situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coach's Challenge — last-two-minutes restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: In the last two minutes of the fourth period or the last two minutes of overtime, a called out-of-bounds violation or called goaltending/basket interference violation will not be challengeable and instead will be exclusively triggered by on-court referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates an exclusive on-court-referee jurisdiction for those event types in the final two minutes of regulation or overtime; teams cannot use their challenge for those events in that timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coach's Challenge — initiation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To initiate a challenge, a team must immediately call a legal timeout and the head coach must immediately signal for a challenge by twirling his/her finger toward the referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two simultaneous conditions: (1) immediate legal timeout request, and (2) an immediate visible head-coach signal (twirling finger). Both are required to start the challenge process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coach's Challenge — delay-of-game removes challenge right
rubrics_metrics.description: A team loses its right to challenge the preceding call if it incurs a delay-of-game violation prior to initiating the challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a delaying infraction occurs before the challenge is properly initiated, the team forfeits its ability to challenge that play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coach's Challenge — definition of 'immediately' for window to challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: When officials confer to determine the appropriate call, the window of time within which a team must “immediately” challenge the call starts after the officials provide the negatively affected team notice of the final ruling on the play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'immediate' timeout/signal requirement is measured from when officials give the affected team notice of the final ruling; this clarifies when the challenge window opens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coach's Challenge — excessive timeout penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: If a team attempts to challenge an event with no remaining timeouts, the team is charged an excessive timeout, for which the penalty is a technical foul, and no challenge will take place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempting to challenge without timeouts results in a technical foul and the challenge is not conducted; administrative/strategic consequence for mis-timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coach's Challenge — timeout charged for non-reviewable events
rubrics_metrics.description: If a team calls a timeout to challenge an event that may not be reviewed, the team will be charged a timeout but retain its challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team loses the timeout even if play is not reviewable, but keeps the right to use its one challenge later (if still applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coach's Challenge — standard of evidence to overturn
rubrics_metrics.description: As with other replay reviews, in order to overturn the event as called on the floor, there must be clear and conclusive visual evidence that the call was incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden for overturn is high: only clear and conclusive visual evidence will suffice; this parallels other replay-review standards used by the league.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media contacts and communications protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: NBA Communications contacts listed (names, titles, phone numbers, emails) for League Operations Communications and Team & Basketball Communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the official points of contact for media inquiries about officiating and league operations; contact details are given for timely communications and clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting officiating resources (court diagram & hand signals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The media guide includes an Official NBA Court Diagram and Referee Hand Signals sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are presented as visual/technical reference materials to assist media and others in accurately describing and depicting officiating-related matters.
